title: Obsolete authentication failure clears a newer successful account
evidence: REPRODUCED: real Swift SDK / controlled HTTP
problem: A delayed failed sign-in for A calls endSession after B has successfully signed in. The isolated SDK probe confirms B becomes unauthenticated. Similar unguarded failure paths exist for Apple/restore and require tracing; those additional paths were not separately reproduced.
required_action: Give authentication attempts an explicit generation. Recheck both successful and failed completions before publishing identity, clearing a session, reporting an error or bootstrapping. Preserve the central transition order.
closure_check: Hold A failure, complete B sign-in, release A: B remains authenticated and retains its projection and error state. Cover the shared failure funnel rather than duplicating every provider test.

title: Private presentation state survives direct A-to-B transition
problem: RootView keeps the ContentView branch while isAuthenticated remains true. Discover has a local model and one-time initial load; Concierge holds conversation, selections, drafts and tasks. Store clearing alone does not clear these private presentation copies. The historical review assumed sign-out unmounting covered all transitions.
required_action: Scope private presentation lifetime to account generation, reset drafts/conversations/selections and cancel work, then reload for the new account. Choose targeted resets or an account-scoped subtree identity; avoid resetting all public caches and approved navigation unnecessarily.
closure_check: An integrated A-to-B journey with populated Discover, Concierge and an open private sheet reveals no A data or drafts, and B loads once. Same-user token refresh preserves legitimate state.

title: Friend activity can return after same-account club revocation
evidence: REPRODUCED: real Swift SDK / controlled HTTP
problem: invalidateFriendProjection clears count work, but fetchFriendActivityForTitle checks account identity only. A delayed response from revoked membership is returned. The detail section retains activity and only keys its task to mediaId; if another club remains, hasClubs remains true.
required_action: Add a permission/membership generation to Social snapshots, reject stale responses and reset/refetch the section on permission change. Distinguish account change, membership change and public catalog lifetime.
closure_check: Hold activity, revoke one club while keeping another, release: revoked friend comments/progress are neither returned nor rendered. Current authorized friend activity can be reloaded.

title: Successful private mutation completions bypass account guards
evidence: REPRODUCED for Social; SOURCE-CONFIRMED for Club success-side effects
problem: An A comment response is handed out after B becomes current. Social mutations do not capture/check context. Club create/join and success cache evictions have incomplete context checks. Taste can return accepted=true for an ended account even though its Library hook is guarded. This contradicts the claim that every private completion is fenced.
required_action: Capture account and applicable permission scope for every private operation. Recheck before success-side effects, errors, refreshes and returning private outcomes. The view must also reject obsolete completion before clearing a newer draft. Audit the complete method inventory, not just the reproduced example.
closure_check: Delayed old-account success and failure cannot change the new account caches, drafts, loading/error state, selections or routes. Reuse the existing SDK harness for representative mutation families.

title: Reminder cleanup can remove newer-account notifications
evidence: SOURCE-CONFIRMED race; notification scheduling interleaving not executed
problem: Session cleanup awaits channel removal or pending notification lookup and then deletes unscoped airing-* IDs. A new account can become current during either suspension. The nil-account check before an await does not protect the later delete.
required_action: Bind notification identifiers and cleanup to owner/generation, or serialize the ownership transition safely. Recheck after asynchronous lookups; do not remove a newer owner marker. Keep restored-own-account reminders and sign-out ordering correct.
closure_check: Pause old cleanup, establish B and its reminders, resume cleanup: B reminders and ownership survive. Ended A reminders are removed.

title: Tracking cache invalidation is undone by an in-flight parse
evidence: REPRODUCED: real Swift SDK / controlled HTTP
problem: dropTrackingCopies clears only completed cache entries. A parse already in flight later republishes an old existing_entry response; account context remains valid. Cache TTL is 600 seconds. Reconciliation prefers a provided server existing_entry, so fresh Library knowledge does not necessarily repair the stale copy.
required_action: Introduce a tracking revision for parse loads/cache, cancel or supersede loads on relevant changes, and reject pre-change completion. Define precedence between current Library knowledge and a versioned parser snapshot.
closure_check: Begin parse, make a Library change, release old parse: it cannot repopulate a usable stale cache or drive an outdated Apply preview. A new parse/explicit rebase uses current state.

title: Older club bundle is returned despite a newer accepted cache entry
evidence: SOURCE + existing controlled test prove stale return; screen publication traced
problem: The store refuses to replace a newer cached bundle but returns the older response anyway. ClubDetailView assigns it. The existing test expects PLANNING from the old caller while the cache holds CURRENT, characterizing the undesired behavior.
required_action: Return the accepted newest snapshot or reject superseded loads. Prefer a monotonic request generation to wall-clock ordering. Cover the caller, not only the cache.
closure_check: An old request finishing after the post-write refresh cannot restore an old status/progress/rating in the screen. Rewrite the characterization expectation into the intended invariant.

title: Undo overwrites later edits to fields the import wrote
evidence: REPRODUCED: actual Apply/Undo handlers with controlled database
problem: Import rating 8 to 9, manually edit to 10, Undo restores 8 without warning. modifiedSinceImport compares list_type/progress only, while restoration can write rating and notes. This is retained behavior, not attributed as a new migration regression.
required_action: Compare every field being reverted against the imported after-image, including nullable rating/notes. Perform comparison and conditional change atomically; an application-level read then write still races with a concurrent edit.
closure_check: Later edits to written rating/notes/status/progress survive Undo. Unrelated fields remain untouched. Add one controlled database race for compare-and-revert, not a combinatorial test matrix.

title: Undo resurrects an entry deleted after an update import
evidence: REPRODUCED: actual handlers with controlled database
problem: A current=null row skips the modified-state test and an update with previous_values is restored by upsert. A deliberate deletion after import is reversed silently. Retained behavior.
required_action: Treat absence after an update as a later user change. Specify add/update/remove compensation independently; do not conflate restoring an import with recreating subsequently deleted data.
closure_check: Import update, delete row, Undo: row stays absent and the response explains the skipped compensation. Normal untouched update Undo still works.

title: Apply succeeds when its item journal insert fails
evidence: REPRODUCED: actual handlers / returned PostgREST-shaped error
problem: List write succeeds, import_session_items insert returns an error, Apply ignores it and reports success. Undo reads no journal item, reports success with no reverted rows, and leaves the imported row. Retained defect.
required_action: Make list write plus journal creation a cohesive transaction. Required journal errors must not be best-effort. Checking the error only after the list write does not establish atomicity or recovery.
closure_check: Injected journal failure yields no unjournaled accepted mutation. Successful Apply always has an executable journal. Test the real transaction against PostgreSQL and handler error translation once.

title: Apply ignores session-finalization failure
evidence: REPRODUCED: actual handler / returned database error
problem: Failure of the status update leaves a draft session, yet Apply reports success. Undo then returns No applied session to undo while the row remains. Retained defect.
required_action: Check required state transitions and tie them to recoverable transaction outcomes. Distinguish required accounting from optional analytics. Prevent duplicate execution after a lost acknowledgment.
closure_check: Failed finalization cannot be reported as completed Apply. Retrying uses the established operation identity and resolves the same outcome without duplicated business writes.

title: Partially successful Apply cannot be undone and is hidden by UI
evidence: REPRODUCED: actual handlers; UI path SOURCE-CONFIRMED
problem: One valid manga add and one anime conflict produce a persistent successful write and status failed. Undo only searches applied sessions and returns 404. The UI shows generic failure and omits a partial-success summary/action. Retained behavior.
required_action: Choose an explicit coherent transaction contract: atomic all-or-nothing, or item-level partial outcomes with recoverable journal and Undo eligibility. Preserve current callers or deliberately version the contract. Surface accepted items and failed/conflicted items accurately.
closure_check: Mixed input leaves either no accepted writes or an accurately reported, reversible partial result. Retrying never loses the original before-image or silently reclassifies an original add into an unrelated update.

title: Failed Undo is marked cancelled and cannot be retried
evidence: REPRODUCED: actual handlers / transient delete failure
problem: Undo collects a transient per-item error, marks the whole session cancelled anyway, and returns success=false. A retry returns 404 while the row remains. The cancellation update error is also ignored. Retained defect.
required_action: Record per-item compensation state or use a safe transaction. Mark complete only after required work succeeds. Support retry without compensating already-reverted items again.
closure_check: Fail one compensation, remove the fault, retry: unfinished work completes, completed work remains correct, and session state matches the actual result.

title: Identifier clamping changes invalid input into title 1
problem: 0, -4 and null media IDs are accepted as media ID 1 because Number coercion and clamping are used for identity. Retained defect. Other identity/candidate-index coercions deserve the same review.
required_action: Reject non-integer, non-positive, out-of-range or missing identities. Validate status against the supported medium-specific vocabulary. Keep quantity clamping separate from identifier validation.
closure_check: These inputs return validation errors and send no list write. Valid Anime/Manga IDs remain distinct even with the same numeric value.

title: Season/episode annotations overwrite existing user notes
evidence: DOCUMENTED retained behavior; pinned in real handler tests
problem: An import with S/E data and no explicit notes synthesizes S{n}E{m} and writes it over stored anime notes. The new provided-fields-only claim has an exception that can discard authored notes.
required_action: Preserve existing notes when notes were not explicitly edited. Keep structural season/episode annotations separate, or use a reviewed non-destructive representation. Carry this distinction in the edit/journal contract.
closure_check: Existing authored notes survive a progress/season-only import and its Undo. Explicit note edits still apply and compensate correctly.

title: Native UUID casing disagrees with captured list RLS
problem: Swift uuidString is passed as upper-case TEXT; captured RLS compares auth.uid()::text in lower case. The fixture rejects upper-case IDs containing hex letters. A fake backend using the same string for both sides can conceal this mismatch.
required_action: Inspect approved read-only effective policies/data before choosing normalization. Canonicalize at one adapter boundary, preserve supported historical rows, and prepare a forward migration if legacy casing requires it. Do not blanket-rewrite user IDs or production rows.
closure_check: Real SDK request plus qualified RLS accepts the authenticated owner and denies another user, for UUIDs containing letters. Historical casing is handled without duplicate or lost rows.

title: SDK decodes detail while PostgREST sends details
evidence: SOURCE-CONFIRMED and characterized; server still denies forbidden actions
sources: Kuro/Clubs/ClubError.swift or ClubsStore error mapping; supabase-swift Sources/PostgREST/PostgrestError.swift; docs/plans/2026-10-05-modular-architecture-execution-ledger.md
problem: Structured SQL DETAIL codes are lost at decoding in the reviewed SDK. This harms duplicate/membership-loss diagnosis and revocation handling; it does not demonstrate an authorization bypass.
required_action: Use a supported reliable wire code mapping, a justified dependency repair, or a compatible server error shape. Keep one translator and preserve rejection semantics. Do not arbitrarily trust arbitrary text as a membership-loss code.
closure_check: A realistic PostgREST JSON error reaches the typed ClubError and intended revocation behavior. Unknown errors remain unknown, and another account is never revoked by an old error.

title: Synopsis cache mixes Anime/Manga identity and input domains
problem: The same Int dictionary stores description.hashValue keys and bare mediaId keys. Anime 7 and Manga 7 share the explicit ID key; an updated description can reuse old content for the same ID. Sharing hash and ID namespaces is also unnecessary collision risk.
required_action: Use a typed key containing MediaKey plus relevant source revision/input digest and locale. Keep text-only calls in a distinct key case. Expose a small provider/cache seam without requiring live Foundation Models in tests.
closure_check: Equal numeric Anime/Manga IDs and changed input never return each other's cached text. Non-FM devices continue to show the existing fallback safely.

title: Notification delivery permission changes are not reflected in outcomes
evidence: SOURCE-CONFIRMED scheduling contract gap; device behavior UNVERIFIED
problem: Permission is requested only when notDetermined. Scheduling is void and failures are debug-only, so revocation is not represented to callers. The review does not claim an observed delivered notification after denial.
required_action: Make permission/delivery outcome explicit at the notification boundary and recheck authorization when relevant. Preserve approved UI; avoid new prompts on every schedule. Test the existing abstraction and qualify one live notification path separately.
closure_check: Denied/revoked permission cannot be reported as successful delivery or leave misleading state. Authorized scheduling and restored-own-account behavior remain intact.

title: Request timestamps omit a time-zone designator
evidence: CHARACTERIZED wire shape; incorrect live instant NOT demonstrated
sources: KuroTests/CollectionContractTests.swift:37; SDK date encoder / RPC date payloads
problem: The test helper appends Z to SDK timestamps lacking a zone and assumes UTC. This can conceal interpretation differences at PostgreSQL boundaries; no observed production time shift is claimed.
required_action: Define timestamp versus civil-date semantics at each affected API. Use explicit UTC instants where appropriate, or prove the server interpretation under a non-UTC database session. Do not alter display dates indiscriminately.
closure_check: Same instant survives SDK encode, database cast and decode across non-UTC session/device settings. Date-only fields retain their intended civil-date meaning.

title: Batch status updates fan out redundant Collection refreshes
problem: Each batch status mutation triggers the Collection sink, then the view performs an explicit feed fetch. The existing withCollectionRefreshDeferred helper is used by removal but not status updates. Cancelling successive requests still creates avoidable started work.
required_action: Use the existing deferral scope for the batch, retain per-item outcomes and perform one final refresh for the active filter. Do not add a global event framework.
closure_check: A representative batch produces bounded final refresh requests, preserves per-item success/failure reporting and leaves the visible filter correct.

title: Collection card pages are fetched without current view consumers
evidence: SOURCE/DOCUMENTED unused data path; confirm final callers before removal
problem: collectionAnimeItems and collectionMangaItems are fetched and held but no current view reads them according to the caller map. Bootstraps and post-import refreshes can do work the feed-based UI does not use.
required_action: Revalidate callers including flags and prototype-linked production views. Remove unused live reads/state, or integrate them as a justified projection with an actual consumer. Keep card pages required by another approved flow.
closure_check: The remaining Collection state has named real consumers and cold/post-write request counts show no unused page loads. Removal does not break imports or exports.

title: Catalog keeps unwritten legacy paging state and an ineffective export fallback
problem: Legacy animeItems/currentAnimePage/loading fields have no current writer. Imports export reads the always-empty array as a title fallback. The fields suggest a second catalog/list projection that is not real.
required_action: Remove unwritten paging state after confirming callers. Resolve export titles through a typed Catalog reader or established hydrated Library entry path, with bounded batch fetching rather than per-title N+1 requests.
closure_check: Exports contain available real titles; unresolved IDs use an explicit truthful fallback. No stale unused paging state or replacement independent tracking authority remains.

title: Unreachable GenreHub keeps a large legacy rail family alive
problem: GenreHubView has no current construction; roughly 300 lines of rail methods and two section types exist mainly for it. fetchTrendingAnime still has a real AuthView consumer and must not be swept away with the dead family.
required_action: Trace all route/flag/preview/operational callers. Locally retire unreachable source or assign an approved reachable consumer; do not add a new product route merely to justify keeping code. Preserve actually used trending behavior.
closure_check: Each retained Discovery API has a current consumer; removed code has no remaining compiled references and the existing Auth experience is preserved.

title: TasteDeck and its outbox UI are not mounted in production
problem: ContentView mounts TastePicksView; TasteDeckView has no construction in Kuro. Tests of its model/outbox do not establish behavior of the actual mounted Taste surface. Historical inventory still describes a deck at pager index 0.
required_action: Map the current approved Taste capability and real signal writers. Remove obsolete unreachable code if confirmed, or integrate only if the product authority requires it. Ensure the actual mounted surface uses the one signal owner.
closure_check: A real mounted Taste journey verifies signal ownership, errors and navigation. The inventory accurately names the reachable UI and no second signal writer is introduced.

title: The declared non-FM stub is unused and fallback is untested
problem: StubFMProvider is never instantiated. The live AppleFMService availability guard returns nil, which is different from proving a functioning injected fallback. Existing documentation can imply more fallback coverage than exists.
required_action: Use the existing FMProvider seam where it makes caller behavior testable; test unavailable and failed-provider outcomes. Remove unused stub code if it serves no consumer, or wire it into tests. Preserve current nil/no-assist behavior.
closure_check: Classification, disambiguation, synopsis and collection-search consumers work without FM and without an extra loading trap or unintended server classifier.

title: Three parser defects are pinned as green characterization cases
problem: parser_en_009 and parser_de_012 split Steins;Gate on semicolon; parser_de_022 drops the German perfect-tense progress phrase bis Kapitel 200. Current-output pins can keep the gate green while the intended input still fails.
required_action: Repair title-preserving segmentation and the progress extraction in production rules. Update the specific defect pins to intended outcomes, retaining protected supported inputs. Avoid another copied parser in tests.
closure_check: The three corpus cases pass the intended behavior through production rules and an import integration example targets the correct title and progress.

title: Two German mood cases route to fallback instead of intended modes
problem: router_de_005 romantisches and router_de_029 schauriges route to premium_picks. They are pinned production outputs, not proof of the expected mood behavior.
required_action: Define the intended inflection matching in the deterministic router, keeping the closed mode vocabulary and narration-only server AI policy. Resolve the two cases without a broad heuristic rewrite.
closure_check: The exact German inputs reach the accepted modes; existing EN/DE corpus expectations remain valid or explicitly adjudicated.

title: Parser corpus disagreements have unresolved acceptance meaning
problem: Ten product-question cases are pinned and four corrected expectations exist only in the test while original corpus data differs. IDs: de_050,en_046,en_039,de_037,en_040,de_038,en_055,de_046,de_052,de_018; corrections de_013,en_011,en_025,de_004. Not all disagreement is a demonstrated parser bug.
required_action: Adjudicate each case against accepted import semantics, document the outcome and keep the canonical fixtures/test annotations consistent. Do not claim zero defects by re-expecting undesired output.
closure_check: Each listed case has an explicit intended outcome and rationale. A corpus gate distinguishes genuine defects from accepted semantic choices without silently modifying all expectations.

title: clarify_v2 off allows parser-ambiguous auto-Apply
problem: Concierge can auto-apply parser-ambiguous lines when clarify_v2 is off; Profile uses a stricter entrypoint. Adaptation ambiguity still blocks, so these are different ambiguities. The divergence is intentional in the code but weakens a broad safe-import claim.
required_action: Use the active product contract to define write-safe ambiguity. Default to requiring review for material uncertainty about title/status/progress; preserve harmless wording ambiguity only with an explicit rule. Centralize named rules and document any intentional surface difference.
closure_check: An ambiguous title/adaptation or materially uncertain mutation cannot silently apply. Concierge and Profile each have an explicit tested acceptance policy for both flag states.

title: Parse and Apply normalize aliases differently
problem: Parser normalization strips additional verbs and rating expressions; Apply normalization does not. An alias recorded at Apply can miss the lookup key used by Parse.
required_action: Extract one shared production alias-normalization rule used by both paths. Assess existing persisted aliases before changing matching; preserve valid provider/source identity and avoid name-only adaptation linkage.
closure_check: Record then look up representative EN/DE/rating-bearing aliases through actual consumers: keys agree. Existing aliases have a compatible read path or prepared migration strategy.

title: Rate-limit lookup errors fail open
evidence: REPRODUCED for Apply; analogous paths SOURCE-CONFIRMED
problem: A returned rate-limit RPC error with data=null is ignored. Apply continues and writes successfully in the added actual-handler probe. Undo/Parse/Resolve similarly test allowed=false without checking error. This is retained behavior.
required_action: Define the limiter as a required gate for protected work. A missing/error result must not permit a write or paid provider call. Return a retryable typed failure distinct from an actual 429 denial; keep legitimate anonymous/public endpoint contracts explicit.
closure_check: Limiter error produces no business write/provider charge, explicit denial remains 429 with Retry-After, and a valid allowed result proceeds.

title: Captured account context is not an SDK credential lease
evidence: SOURCE-CONFIRMED design risk; cross-account server write NOT reproduced
owner: Identity / request adapters / Imports / Taste / Social
problem: Private callers share one SDK client. The SDK obtains the current token during request adaptation, whereas app context was captured earlier. Unstructured/delayed work can reach dispatch after a transition. Result guards alone do not prove obsolete work cannot send or be attributed to a new account. Explicit list user filters offer extra RLS defense; JWT-derived RPC writers differ.
required_action: Trace token acquisition and dispatch for each private mutation family. Bind the dispatched credential identity to the initiating account, reject obsolete context before dispatch/retries, and cancel queued work. Do not fix this by trusting a client-supplied user_id. Use a supported request broker/scoped transport only if necessary.
closure_check: A controlled pre-dispatch account-switch test proves no A-originated queued mutation is sent as B. Do not mark a merely late response test as proof of credential binding.

title: Private club raw votes/reactions/member rows bypass aggregate privacy
problem: Membership-only SELECT policies let members read raw per-user rows directly. Privacy gating and anonymous counts in RPC responses do not protect direct table reads.
required_action: Design a minimal privacy-preserving aggregate boundary with explicit caller membership checks and safe search_path/grants. Restrict raw personal rows while retaining necessary approved member metadata. A SECURITY DEFINER conversion must not accidentally reveal private individual tracking fields.
closure_check: Another member cannot read forbidden raw identities/votes/reactions/progress by direct SELECT, and intended aggregate totals still work for private/status/progress levels.

title: Removal is not sticky and departed votes/reactions remain in counts
problem: Owner/admin removal or leave deletes membership, but the shared invite code still permits rejoin. Departed votes/reactions remain in aggregates and raw rows. Leave dialog promises stronger finality than this implements.
required_action: Define removal separately from voluntary leave. Proposed safe default: owner-removed users require explicit restoration; voluntary leave can rejoin with a valid invite and accurate copy. Decide whether departed activity is deleted or excluded from current-member counts. Enforce the rule server-side.
closure_check: Removed user cannot immediately rejoin with the old code; a valid explicitly restored user can. Leave copy and retained/excluded activity match the chosen contract. No new removal UI is required just to enforce existing backend operations.

title: Current RLS makes cross-member bundle status counts incomplete
problem: Bundle runs SECURITY INVOKER and list RLS exposes only caller rows. In the fixture, three of four members track an item but member_status_counts reflects only the caller. Restricting SELECT further without changing aggregation also reduces polls/reactions/member count.
required_action: Implement authorized aggregate computation together with F34. Individual data remains subject to sharing level. Do not regard a blanket SECURITY DEFINER flip as a complete repair: it also enables previously hidden cross-member data.
closure_check: Expected counts are correct for multiple members while private individual tracking remains hidden. Test raw access and aggregate output together.

title: Account deletion bypasses club ownership-transfer and current-orphan cleanup
evidence: FIXTURE-REPRODUCED; newest cleanup RPC qualification outstanding
problem: In the exercised fixture a shared club loses its owner and a solo club becomes an orphan after the sweep already ran. leave_club has lifecycle logic account deletion bypasses. The fixture uses an older cleanup RPC body, so the exact current hosted result remains unverified.
required_action: Inspect/qualify the effective cleanup RPC and establish one club lifecycle operation for deletion, ownership transfer and empty-club cleanup. Handle current victim clubs explicitly rather than relying on the next unrelated deletion sweep.
closure_check: Deleting an owner preserves a shared club with valid ownership or the explicitly approved ownerless policy, and a solo club is cleaned safely. Other members' content is preserved.

title: Account deletion has a concurrent-write cleanup gap
problem: After TEXT list cleanup, a still-authenticated concurrent request inserts a row; deleting auth.users does not cascade that list row. The probe confirms the survivor. Notes-only updates under simulated deleted-user claims also work; a normal new insert after deletion is indirectly blocked by a taste FK. Live acceptance of deleted-user JWTs was not proven.
required_action: Establish a database-enforced deletion/write barrier and compatible ownership/cascade strategy for all user-keyed relations, including legacy TEXT rows. Coordinate cleanup with concurrent mutations. Preserve retryability and never rely solely on local sign-out or a final best-effort sweep.
closure_check: Controlled competing write cannot leave private data after successful deletion. Interrupted deletion can retry safely. Qualified Auth/Storage behavior remains a separate gate.

title: Orphan sweep count/delete race can destroy a newly joined club
problem: Sweep sees zero members, another user joins, then the unconditional service-role DELETE removes the club and cascades the new membership. The global sweep can affect clubs unrelated to the currently deleting user. Retained pattern.
required_action: Use a database operation coordinated with joins and a revalidated deletion condition under the appropriate lock, or remove the global sweep from the request and use a safe separate cleanup owner. A stale pre-read is not authorization to delete.
closure_check: Join between observation and deletion preserves the joined club. Truly empty eligible clubs can still be cleaned. Exercise the concurrency boundary once with two database sessions.

title: Legacy user_lists view can expose another user's rows
evidence: FIXTURE reconstruction demonstrates risk; live view existence/options UNVERIFIED
problem: The reconstructed legacy view without security_invoker allows user 2 to see user 1 rows. It is absent from the baseline capture and the hardening migration does not replay, so this is not a claim that the deployed view currently leaks.
required_action: Inspect effective view existence/options/grants in the qualified environment. Preserve invoker semantics or retire an unused view through an approved forward change. Include view access in the authorization contract, not just table policies.
closure_check: Other-user and anonymous view reads are denied/empty as intended, and owner access works through the exact effective view or its documented replacement.

title: Three authorization repairs are prepared only, not qualified deployed state
evidence: FIXTURE red/green evidence; hosted status UNVERIFIED
problem: Prepared fixes address role escalation via UPDATE, unauthorized direct rail INSERT, and comment reaction visibility. The green fixture includes these files by default. Effective live policies may differ and no deployment has been performed.
required_action: Recheck each precondition/grant and prepare cohesive forward migrations. Keep files outside the deploy path until authorized. Preserve intended sharing-level edits, admin actions and visible comment reactions. Account for all broad PUBLIC/table/column grants.
closure_check: Old qualified schema reproduces each denied action; fixed qualified schema rejects it and allows legitimate operations. Applied-state claims require explicit deployment and post-check evidence.

title: Membership revocation lacks a server event and subscriptions are broad
problem: club_members is not in the reviewed Realtime publication; rail/vote/reaction subscriptions are unfiltered, with only polls filtered by club. Removed members may keep a cached bundle until a failing request or TTL. The in-memory invalidation method cannot react to a signal never received.
required_action: Provide a scoped authorized revocation/invalidation path and filter subscriptions where the real table schema permits. Restrict event payloads consistently with privacy policy and prevent stale channel callbacks from publishing. Use bounded refetch of aggregates where private raw events cannot be delivered.
closure_check: A member removed externally loses private state/subscription promptly according to an explicit contract. Rejoin/old teardown does not drop the current channel. Qualify actual Realtime delivery separately from fake channel tests.

title: Database fixture is an incomplete effective schema
evidence: REPLAY MEASURED: 176 applied / 62 failed baseline-first, including prepared files
problem: 321 passing assertions cover a partial audited fixture. taste_tag_stats is absent and the newest delete_user_concierge_data body does not replay. Strict replay measured 130 applied/108 failed including 3 prepared files; baseline-post measured 2/4. Do not confuse 235 historical files with 238 attempted files.
required_action: Prepare a qualified non-production schema strategy with required seed dependencies/effective view/function bodies. Preserve historical migrations/checksums. Add a setup completeness check for the objects the slice depends on, and report replay failure distinctly from RLS test success.
closure_check: Changed authorization/transaction tests execute against the required effective objects and roles, including the latest cleanup RPC and taste isolation. Missing objects keep their gates BLOCKED.

title: Storage, GoTrue and live PostgREST behavior are not established
problem: The fixture stubs auth/storage and simulates Auth deletion as superuser. In-process HTTP responses exercise the SDK but not a running PostgREST server. Real grants, HTTP error mapping, Storage ownership and GoTrue session/token semantics remain unqualified.
required_action: Use an approved disposable/local full stack or non-production target, never production as substitute. Keep unit/fixture/hosted labels distinct. Prepare recovery commands if prerequisites are unavailable; finish independent source work without declaring these gates passed.
closure_check: Representative real-stack auth, owner mutation, permission error and deletion paths match contracts. A missing stack is BLOCKED, not PASS and not a reason to deploy early.

title: Hardened deletion requires unverified deployed prerequisites
problem: Required deletes now include anime_comments/manga_comments; service_role DELETE grants, table column types and the media bucket have not been verified against an effective deployed-equivalent schema. A mismatch would make deletion fail for every affected user.
required_action: Run approved read-only prerequisite checks and prepare any missing grants/schema changes explicitly. Keep required failures visible and Auth deletion last. Do not weaken cleanup to make a happy-path test pass.
closure_check: All required relations, grants and bucket exist with expected ownership semantics; missing prerequisites fail safely and are resolved before any deployment approval.

title: Several auth legs and outbound auth headers lack SDK-level qualification
problem: Launch restore, sign-up, Apple sign-in, same-user callback setSession and SDK event mapping have mainly funnel-entry evidence. Authorization/apikey headers are not asserted in current adapter tests. Existing email tests do not qualify every distinct credential path.
required_action: Test each distinct SDK credential/session mechanism once at the existing HTTP seam with controlled responses. Assert relevant identity/headers and stale-attempt behavior. Reuse shared funnel tests for common cleanup rather than multiplying provider permutations.
closure_check: Actual SDK mapping and persisted-session behavior are checked where supported. Tests use fixture credentials only and verify a nonzero executed count.

title: All sixteen integrated UI journeys remain unqualified
evidence: DOCUMENTED; review probes were unit tests, not UI journeys
problem: Pure RoutePolicy tests do not establish real sheet presenters, nested navigation, cold/warm deep links, swipe arbitration, filter selection or approved layouts. The review's four simulator SDK probes do not close these journeys.
required_action: Create a safe fixture-only app/launch configuration and perform the sixteen listed journey checks, grouping automation by distinct wiring pattern. Use deterministic waits and selective visual inspection; avoid a sprawling screenshot suite.
closure_check: Each documented journey has a result on the current source. Correct detail/editor/club appears, nested presenters and deep links work, swipe does not open a card, and approved composition is preserved.

title: Test host can initialize production configuration
evidence: SOURCE-CONFIRMED possibility; no production request incident asserted
problem: The unit-test host constructs AppComposition.shared and starts launch restore with the ordinary production configuration. Per-test StubSupabase clients isolate test requests but do not necessarily isolate the host app. The review used an isolated copied app with invalid fixture host/key.
required_action: Add a supported test-only composition/configuration path selected before singleton creation, isolated SDK persistence and a network-deny guard. Keep production builds unable to enter it accidentally. Do not remove actual lifecycle behavior from the test path being qualified.
closure_check: Running unit/UI verification cannot contact production or inherit real-account tokens. A test intentionally attempting external production access is rejected locally before network dispatch.

title: Critical handler tests are not part of the normal gate path
problem: run_all invokes parser/router tests but not Apply, Undo or delete-account handler/deletion suites. The DB fixture is also separate. A normal green gate can therefore miss the business-critical failures this review reproduced.
required_action: Wire the existing focused Deno suites into the standard local/CI verification path. Make DB qualification an explicit separately labeled gate if setup differs. Reuse existing tests; do not duplicate them as another test framework.
closure_check: A meaningful Apply/Undo/deletion regression fails the documented gate command. Missing prerequisites produce an explicit failure/BLOCKED report, and skipped gates cannot be summarized as complete.

title: Screen-level request and subscription baselines are missing
problem: Counts are pinned for selected owner flows, not cold/warm/remount screen journeys. One SDK client is a static check. Post-import view refreshes can duplicate sink work, and repeated mount/subscription paths remain incompletely measured.
required_action: Instrument existing controlled transports for representative screen cold/warm/remount and mutation flows. Resolve unexplained increases and duplicate subscriptions. Keep a small counter-based assertion set, not a new analytics platform or large load benchmark.
closure_check: Each representative wiring pattern has a bounded justified request/channel count; batch/import paths do not multiply redundant refreshes.

title: Active backend handlers remain mixed orchestration boundaries
problem: Recommend remains 1,806 lines with an approximately 1,300-line serve closure; parser search/alias/current-entry orchestration remains in index; manga enrichment remains 2,088 lines; bulk importers 747/770. Low churn or lack of an offline consumer does not close actual divergent policy/provider/repository/run seams.
required_action: Complete the function-specific extraction matrix below, preserving slugs and contracts. Entry adapters bind environment/request dependencies and call testable run handlers. Put pure matching/selection rules beside typed repositories/provider transports, without mandatory generic layers.
closure_check: Every active backend capability has a cohesive run entry, production policy tests and one controlled failure-path handler/run test. No required seam is deferred solely because the old file rarely changes.

title: Operational workers were indexed rather than semantically extracted/verified
owner: Synopsis / safety / providers / media relations / operations
problem: The migration preserves and indexes worker paths but does not exercise lock, checkpoint, cursor, retry, report or worker orchestration boundaries. Stable wrapper paths do not require keeping all internals monolithic.
required_action: Keep wrapper/label/report compatibility and extract only real internal seams using existing language patterns. Update Swift compile commands to include actual supporting sources. Introduce a controlled offline run seam and ensure production wrappers invoke it.
closure_check: Each active worker has one success and one representative interrupted/provider-failure run proving cleanup/checkpoint/report behavior. No live provider or production write is used as a unit-test substitute.

title: Central models and RPC parameter collections retain cross-capability editing coupling
problem: SupabaseModels is 1,297 lines and combines value vocabulary with legacy/projection/provider concerns. Roughly 30 RPC parameter types have single-owner consumers spread across capabilities, keeping multiple owners editing one file. Large size alone is not the defect.
required_action: Move owner-private request/response types beside their adapter; put truly shared catalog/media values in one neutral contract home. Move provider policy to Providers. Preserve a single canonical model definition and legacy decoding compatibility.
closure_check: A capability-specific RPC change edits its capability and tests, not unrelated parameter bundles. No duplicate Anime/Manga/MediaKey model or SDK type leaks into UI/domain APIs.

title: In-app feature boundaries are largely conventional, not enforced
problem: The three package graph is compiler-checked. Other capability owners share the app module, and six regex rules cover selected forbidden patterns rather than arbitrary feature-internal access or all dependency edges. This does not demonstrate that actual cycles exist; it weakens the zero-forbidden-access claim.
required_action: Define a small explicit capability API/dependency manifest; hide implementations using existing access control and enforce cross-capability references with a focused check, or compile a boundary where useful. Permit composition and narrow neutral contracts, not blanket cross-feature access.
closure_check: A representative forbidden reference in a scratch copy fails the gate; valid API calls pass; all actual edges have an owner/rationale and no cycle. Avoid a custom general-purpose architecture compiler.

title: Private workflows remain in large rendering files
evidence: SOURCE-CONFIRMED; some pure-rule extraction is already complete
priority: P2 required where lifetime/ordering defects need it
problem: Clarification/routing/preselection rules and shared detail chrome were extracted and should stay closed. Conversation Apply/Undo sequencing, draft state and multiple task handles remain private view logic. Discover and ClubDetail publish private snapshots in view state; Auth welcome artwork has a separate update/task lifetime.
required_action: Extract a session-local workflow model where necessary to make sequencing, cancellation and reset testable; keep SwiftUI rendering and established approved layouts. Isolate Auth welcome artwork as a presentation component. Do not mandate a view-model class for every simple screen.
closure_check: Actual views consume the new workflow APIs; private state/tasks have one lifecycle owner; rendering files contain no duplicated mutation/reconciliation policy. D1-D3 and existing route extractions are not redone needlessly.

title: Keep-cohesive waivers sometimes use weak evidence
evidence: DOCUMENTED reviewer dissent / architecture acceptance issue
problem: No offline consumer, no recent commits, or no existing test is used to waive backend seams. The Recommend remainder is explicitly called the weakest keep in the large-file review. These facts do not show shared authority, lifetime or failure policy.
required_action: Reassess large active files by owner, invariant, state lifetime, consumers, external boundaries and meaningful failures. Keep genuinely cohesive code regardless of length; split concrete divergent responsibilities now under the expanded whole-codebase scope.
closure_check: Each large active file has a short inspectable cohesion decision with source evidence. A required split cannot be relabeled optional to obtain completion.

title: Operational root assumptions disagree with this checkout
problem: Several installers/runners and the unified dashboard hardcode /Applications/Kuro. The canonical checkout here is /Users/max/Kuro-Anime-App; CI/CD derives its current repo root while the dashboard reads another report root. The review does not claim installed jobs on another host are broken.
required_action: Use one task-specific overridable project-root resolution mechanism, preserve legacy installed paths through compatible wrappers/configuration and verify report-root agreement. Do not reinstall launchd jobs or mutate installed credentials without authorization.
closure_check: Offline configuration checks in the canonical checkout and a relocated scratch copy resolve the same intended workers/reports; existing documented labels/ports/default overrides remain compatible.

title: Media-relations configuration depends on other pipelines' credential plists
problem: The runner obtains SUPABASE variables from other pipelines' installed plists. Removing an unrelated pipeline/label can break credential discovery, undermining independent module removal.
required_action: Define explicit media-relations configuration with compatible fallback during migration. Document which settings are shared public config and which are credentials. Preserve values; do not print secrets or change installed credentials by inference.
closure_check: Media-relations configuration resolves without requiring another pipeline to be installed. Existing configured runs preserve credential precedence and fail clearly when required settings are absent.

title: Local CD deploys production by default
problem: DEPLOY_SUPABASE defaults to 1 and invokes linked db push/functions deploy. A modularity verification task must not accidentally run it as a generic local check.
required_action: Keep deployment separate from verification. Make non-deploy validation explicit/safe and require an intentional deployment entry/flag under project approval rules. Inspect installed scheduler invocation before changing default behavior; no deployment in this task.
closure_check: The documented verification path has no remote writes. Production deployment requires explicit authority and displays the exact target/actions; existing approved automation changes are reviewed separately.

title: Pre-commit checks are not active in this clone
evidence: CURRENT local config check: core.hooksPath unset
problem: The hooks directory exists but is not configured as active here. Documentation should not imply secrets/migration-name checks run automatically on commit. Explicit run_all checks still exist.
required_action: Document and provide the supported opt-in hook setup, or use the established CI gate as the enforced owner. Do not silently change the user's global Git configuration. Ensure the authoritative path runs without relying on local hooks.
closure_check: The selected enforcement path actually rejects a representative secret/migration-name violation in a scratch fixture; local hook status is reported accurately.

title: Authoritative docs and generated source blocks disagree
sources: AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md; CURRENT_APP_STATE.md; CURRENT_APP_STATE_PLAIN.md; IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_Variation1.md; scripts/generate_app_state_sources.js
problem: AGENTS retains deleted service paths and stale counts; generated current-state blocks were deliberately left stale. The source generator may stamp HEAD while embedding dirty source, which is not a complete source identity. The deployment switch description also needs precise true-to-false semantics: it is currently true and should become false after compatible Apply deploy.
required_action: Reconcile the canonical current docs, distinguish historical snapshots, regenerate reviewed/redacted blocks or replace unnecessary source duplication with accurate references under project rules. Record dirty-source digest/source identity rather than HEAD alone. Update status after every actual initiative.
closure_check: No current authority points to deleted production files or presents old counts/behavior as current. Generated evidence matches the actual source and no credentials are embedded. Deployment switch is described accurately.

title: Completion verdict contradicts mandatory gates and reproduced defects
problem: COMPLETE-WITH-DISCLOSED-GAPS claims all code-level gates pass while G4/G5 are partial and G1 now has reproduced failures. Disclosure does not override a mandatory gate. Structural retirement is useful but is not lifecycle qualification.
required_action: Reopen gate statuses, resolve the required work, and apply binary PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT-APPLICABLE evidence. Report local architecture status independently from deployed/release status. Weights cannot compensate for failures.
closure_check: Final verdict follows the actual integrated evidence; all required source work and local gates pass, and unavailable external qualification remains explicitly BLOCKED. No completion headline masks it.

title: Offline/restart guarantees and durable outboxes are absent
evidence: DOCUMENTED product qualification gap, not an automatic new-feature commission
problem: Library projection and Taste outbox are in memory. No durable offline sync or restart proof exists. A modular extraction does not establish those product capabilities; implementing a whole sync platform is not justified solely by modularity.
required_action: Define honest restart/pending-operation semantics and preserve extension seams. Implement persistence only when required by the active approved product contract or to repair loss in an actually reachable existing flow; otherwise record the product gate separately, with no offline-complete claim.
closure_check: Architecture APIs do not promise durability they lack. If durability is required, a focused restart/lost-ack test proves it on the real persistence path.

title: Dormant Groq classifiers conflict with narration-only project policy
problem: Resolve chooses candidates with Groq; realm-describe classifies realm/tone/register/pacing. Current caller maps say Resolve has no app/script consumer and Realm drains are paused/manual. Documentation calling dormancy an exception does not authorize reactivating forbidden classification.
required_action: Confirm actual callers/config/cron and explicitly classify dormant paths. Keep them dormant or prepare local retirement with compatibility notes; do not reactivate them. Any actual classification consumer must follow the approved deterministic/on-device policy, and an exception needs explicit user authority.
closure_check: No active default flow uses server Groq for classification/routing. Dormant/manual paths and removal/deployment boundaries are truthful and owner-assigned.

title: Resolve leaks budget reservations on provider failure
evidence: SOURCE-CONFIRMED; provider failure not separately executed
problem: User/global reservations precede groqResolve; finalization happens only after it succeeds. A thrown provider call jumps to the outer catch without releasing those reservations. Reserve RPC errors also deserve fail-closed review. The function is currently documented dormant.
required_action: If retained as callable code, put reservation lifecycle in one run owner with finally-based compensation/actual-use accounting and checked required outcomes. Respect F64; do not enable the forbidden provider just to exercise a test.
closure_check: A controlled provider throw or denied second reservation leaves no leaked reservation. A successful call accounts for actual usage once, without contacting Groq in tests.

title: Image mirroring has unbounded fetch and payload-selected storage target
evidence: SOURCE-CONFIRMED risk; no abuse incident demonstrated
problem: fetch(url) has no explicit timeout/response-size cap/host allowlist; blob materialization can consume unbounded resources. Bucket comes from payload. A secret gate limits callers but does not define a safe resource/target contract.
required_action: Extract the mirror run and bounded provider/storage adapters. Define approved source hosts/redirect handling, content type/size limits, timeouts and allowed destination bucket/path. Preserve existing authorized sources and report failures without erasing valid prior URLs.
closure_check: Controlled oversized, timeout, redirect-to-unapproved-host and invalid-bucket cases fail safely; valid catalog images mirror once with bounded concurrency and consistent cursor/report behavior.

title: AniList import endpoint has a documented unresolved type error

title: Consolidated outbound URL validation intentionally changed edge behavior

problem: Duplicate validators were successfully removed, but accepted/rejected edge URLs changed. The completion report lists this as a retained compatibility gap. Consolidation alone does not approve every behavior delta.

closure_check: Representative previously valid catalog/provider links still open correctly, malformed/unsupported targets are rejected, and flag-off/catalog fallback works in an integrated detail journey.

title: Dead request/presentation types and misleading file names remain

Unused StubFMProvider is tracked separately under F26. These are navigation/maintenance gaps, not production incidents.

problem: The 169-row manifest inventories Swift app/package/tests, while backend/SQL/scripts rely on separate indexes, many baseline-derived. A file owner alone does not name mutable state, caller/write path, interface or dependency. All production paths need a coherent current view for full-codebase completion.

Classify active/dormant/legacy/generated/prototype assets explicitly; preserve prototypes. Link actual APIs/state/write owners rather than merely listing folders.
